title: Transformation Gallery
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Compare six common transformations on synthetic data, study the before and after plots of each one, tune the Box-Cox lambda, and add zeros and negative values to see where each transformation is undefined.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to compare the effects of the log, square root, reciprocal, square, Box-Cox, and standardizing transformations on the shape of data and state where each transformation is defined.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Gallery of worked examples with before and after plots, one tunable parameter, and a stress test of each transformation's domain
keyQuestions: Why does the log pull in a long right tail while standardizing leaves the tail exactly as it was?
Which transformations fail on a zero, and which fail on a negative number?
How are the square root, the log, and the reciprocal related to the Box-Cox family?
commonMisconceptions: Standardizing makes data normal (it changes the center and the scale but never the shape).
The log works on any numeric column (it is undefined at 0 and for negative values).
A transformation changes the information in the data (it changes the scale on which the same values are measured).
assessmentOpportunities: Given three short descriptions (monthly sales that grow by a fixed percentage, counts of website errors per hour, and two features measured in dollars and in years that will go into a ridge model), students choose a transformation for each, justify it, and say what would happen if the column contained a zero.
